recognize_zh: 寬厚的骨小樑表面可見多核蝕骨細胞（箭頭）貼附在吸收凹陷（Howship lacunae）內，形成蝕骨細胞沿骨緣排列；髓腔中有一小島造血細胞及周圍紡錘狀基質，與骨質硬化病的骨髓變化相符。
features: Thickened, irregular bony trabeculae with scalloped surfaces
Multinucleated osteoclasts with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm sitting in resorption bays along the bone surface (arrows)
Intertrabecular island of mixed hematopoietic cells surrounded by loose spindle-cell stroma
Small lymphoid-appearing cell clusters adjacent to trabeculae
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy at intermediate magnification shows thickened, irregular trabeculae with scalloped surfaces. Multiple multinucleated osteoclasts are present in Howship lacunae along trabecular surfaces, producing osteoclastic rimming. The intertrabecular space contains a cellular island of mixed hematopoietic elements surrounded by loose fibrous stroma. In conjunction with the osteosclerosis and radiographic findings, these features are consistent with osteopetrosis, in which osteoclasts may be numerous but functionally defective.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytes have a single hyperlobated nucleus and lie within the marrow cavity, whereas osteoclasts are truly multinucleated and sit in resorption bays on bone.
Hyperparathyroidism shows tunneling resorption into trabeculae with marrow fibrosis and elevated PTH, rather than dense sclerotic bone in an infant.
Pagetic osteoclasts are huge with dozens of nuclei and accompany mosaic cement lines in older adults.
Mastocytosis forms paratrabecular aggregates of spindled CD117+/tryptase+ mast cells, not multinucleated osteoclasts.
